F1.Prediction Service: Receives the transaction, fetches features, runs the active model, returns within 100 ms.
F1.Decision Policy Engine: Maps score to allow / review / block with per-merchant thresholds and hard rules.
F1.Online Feature Store: Sub-5 ms feature reads are what make the 100 ms budget possible.
F1.Stream Feature Processor: Computes the velocity / decline-rate aggregates the model scores on; BIN lookup integration.
F1.Prediction Logger: Every scored request is logged with model version asynchronously; the only writer of the prediction log that F3/F4/F6 consume.
F1.Model Rollout Controller: Loads the approved production model from the registry so the service has an active model (basic load; shadow/canary split is F6).

F2.Case Review UI: The analyst screen: score, top contributing features, history, verdict.
F2.Label Joiner: Matches analyst verdicts to logged predictions and writes the labels table.
F2.Prediction Service: Must compute per-feature contributions for the case view; no §6 component produces explanations today.
F2.Prediction Logger: Must persist the contributions alongside score/decision so the case view can read them later.

F3.Label Joiner: Pulls the daily SFTP chargeback feed, matches by transaction id, writes labels, computes realized precision/recall per model version.
F3.Model Health UI: Realized precision/recall per model version is only surfaced here; no other feature builds that view.

F4.Drift Monitor: Hourly PSI/KS comparison against training baseline; PagerDuty/Slack paging.
F4.Model Registry: Must hold the production model's training-time feature distributions that are the drift baseline.
F4.Model Health UI: Drift charts per model version are only surfaced here; no other feature builds that view.

F5.Training Pipeline: Orchestrates extract → validate → prepare → train → evaluate; MLflow tracking.
F5.Data Validation Step: A step of the orchestrated pipeline; schema/skew checks on the weekly extract.
F5.Model Validation Gate: Champion/challenger comparison on holdout and per-merchant slices; staging registration rule.
F5.Model Registry: Versions the challenger with lineage and holds it at staging.
F5.Offline Feature Store: Point-in-time-correct training set from feature history and fresh labels.

F6.Model Rollout Controller: Traffic split for shadow, hot-swap on promote.
F6.Model Health UI: Shadow-vs-production comparison and promote / rollback buttons.
F6.Model Registry: Stage transition staging → production / archived with approver.
F6.Prediction Logger: Must write the shadow model's score with its own model version per request so the dashboard can compare.

keyChanges: F1 +Model Rollout Controller: both sets argued the active model must be loaded from the registry by its owning component; a basic load is needed for F1 even without shadow/canary. Accepted.

F2 +Prediction Service, +Prediction Logger: Y pointed out that 'top contributing features' (in the UI Responsibility and the feature text) are produced by no §6 component; the service must compute them and the logger must persist them. Accepted.
F4 +Model Registry: both sets argued the training-time feature distributions exist in the registry only as the drift baseline; the registry must be extended to hold them for F4 to work. Accepted.
F6 +Prediction Logger: both sets argued shadow scoring adds a second score per request under a different model version, which the F1 logger does not write. Accepted.
grayAreas: Training Pipeline in F4 (computing the training-time distributions) — neither set linked it; fits its existing 'records artifacts' responsibility, not counted either way.
Pipeline Trigger in F4 (drift-triggered retraining) — not a listed client feature; would be counted wrong if linked. Neither set did.
patterns: X links Training Data Warehouse to every feature that creates a table (F1 prediction log, F3 labels) by reciting 'partitioning and 2-year retention'; neither feature requires store-specific work — the tables belong to Prediction Logger and Label Joiner. The store exception was applied mechanically as a justification, not because the feature demanded it.

X misses the hidden component work behind a UI responsibility: F2's 'top contributing features' needs Prediction Service to compute explanations and Prediction Logger to persist them; X linked only the UI and the label writer. Y caught it.

Y leaves Model Health UI unlinked in F3 and F4, so the realized precision/recall view and the drift-chart view are priced under no feature (only F6's shadow view is). Y reads the feature text literally ('measured', 'paged') and drops the surfacing work.
Both sets are identical and clean on F5 and F6, and both argued convincingly for Model Rollout Controller in F1, Model Registry in F4 and Prediction Logger in F6 — these moved the key.
